text.tspan: Amazon S3: buckets live in a Region, objects live in buckets
Region: eu-west-1 (a bucket is created in ONE Region)
(no real folders: the key is the FULL path)
Each object: value (body, max 50 TB since Dec 2025, was 5 TB) · metadata
(system + user key/value) · tags (up to 10, Unicode) · version ID (if versioning on)
Single PUT up to 5 GB → bigger needs multipart upload (recommended > 100 MB)
unique across ALL accounts and Regions
only your account can create it, so the
same prefix can be "reused" per Region
not an IP · no uppercase, no underscore
• "One of the main building blocks of AWS": object storage. Objects, not files or blocks (no mounting; you replace an object to change it).
• Bucket names: lowercase, globally unique unless you choose the account regional namespace. The name cannot be changed later.
• Max object 50 TB (older questions say 5 TB). Multipart: up to 10,000 parts, 5 MiB-5 GiB each (last part can be smaller).
• Tags (10 per object, key 128 / value 256 Unicode chars) drive lifecycle rules and IAM conditions; metadata is set at upload.
